newsitem.title: UK: United Utilities sells Keadby Power stake.
newsitem.headline: United Utilities sells Keadby Power stake.

text.p: British water and energy group United Utilities Plc said on Friday it had sold its 50 percent stake in Keadby Power to Scottish Hydro-Electric Plc for 122.7 million stg cash.
The proceeds from the stake, held by United's Norweb subsidiary, would be used to cut borrowings.
The company said the Keadby sale brought the total proceeds from its disposals programme to around 434 million stg.

It said it was holding talks with interested parties to sell Norweb Generation's holdings in two U.S. power stations in Florida and Virginia, its stake in Roosecote power station in Cumbria, north England, and its portfolio of renewable energy projects.
United Utilities said the timing of the disposals of the Retail and Process Equipment Division had cut their contributions to earnings.

"This, together with the downward impact on earnings from the disposal process itself, has resulted in approximately 30 million stg in profit before exceptional items, interest and tax (PBEIT) compared to the pro forma contribution in 1995/96," United Utilities said.
The company said the timing of the receipt of proceeds ensured there was only a marginal interest benefit from the debt reduction. It said in a full year, the disposals would enhance group earnings.
